messages:
maria.hr: Quick thread  Samir is a new hire (start date Oct 1) on his 90-day probation. He requested a bridge day off (Mon Dec 23) that falls inside the company year-end blackout for hiring ops activities. Manager approved but flagged the probation rule about carryover and blackout approvals. Need guidance on whether we can make a one-time carryover exception if his probation prevents accrual enough to cover the day.
devon_mgr: I approved because his role is critical and the team will cover. He only has 6h accrued as of now and needs 8h for the bridge day. He asked if we can advance 2h or mark it as unpaid. What are the rules for advancing PTO for probationers?
hr-bot: Policy note: New hires accrue on a pro-rated schedule and are not eligible for carryover until they reach year-end balance posting. Advance PTO for probationary employees is handled case-by-case; People Ops approval required. See policies: https://redwood.company/policies/pto#new-hires
maria.hr: Key constraints: 1) year-end blackout (Dec 20-31) means we avoid granting unpaid time off that impacts hiring ops headcount unless pre-approved, 2) probationary advances need manager justification and People Ops sign-off. We can offer either an advance of 2h as a loan (must be repaid from future accruals) or allow unpaid time. Which does Devon prefer?
samir.newhire: Hi everyone	I'm happy to take unpaid if that's cleaner. I was hoping not to because I'm traveling with family and it's last-minute plane change fees. If there's a loan option I'd take it and repay over next 3 pay periods. Appreciate any flexibility.
devon_mgr: Can we do loan + note in Lattice that it's an advance for probationary new hire to be repaid over 3 pay periods? That seems reasonable and keeps Samir whole for travel. I'll sign off if People Ops approves.
maria.hr: Process: People Ops needs manager justification on the Lattice request and a signed advance agreement (email suffices) so payroll can set a negative pending accrual entry. If approved we'll tag as "advance_approved" and record repayment schedule. Payroll cutoff for year-end adjustments is Dec 20 so we need docs by then to avoid manual off-cycle.
kelly.payroll: Operational note: to post an advance we create a pending negative accrual token in HRIS; payroll will then deduct agreed amounts across upcoming pay runs. If docs arrive after Dec 20 we can still process but it becomes an off-cycle manual adjustment in January. Also note that blackout for hiring ops is primarily for headcount freezes; single-day coverage exceptions are common with manager and People Ops sign-off.
maria.hr: Recommend timeline: Devon add a manager note on the existing Lattice request: "Manager requests 2h PTO advance for Samir (new hire) to cover bridge day; repayment over 3 pay periods; agreed by employee via email on 12/05". Then Devon DM me a copy of the employee email consent. I'll route for approval and create ticket.
samir.newhire: I'll send the email consent now and cc Devon + Maria. Thanks for handling quickly.
devon_mgr: Note added in Lattice as requested. DMing Maria the consent email.
hr-bot: people-ops ticket created: #PO-43107  maria.hr assigned. Link: https://redwood.company/people-ops/tickets/PO-43107
maria.hr: Approval granted. We'll post the 2h advance as a loan and set repayment for next 3 pay periods. Kelly  can you confirm payroll entries and schedule the deductions?
kelly.payroll: Confirmed  I'll schedule the negative accrual entry now and the deductions across Jan 1, Jan 15, and Jan 31 payrolls. Because this was approved before Dec 20 cutoff it will be in the regular payroll batch.
maria.hr: Closing loop: Samir's bridge day is approved and will not be counted as unpaid. Repayment schedule documented. If anything changes ping People Ops. :thumbsup:
